<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Jordan's ask (2026-08-28, verbatim intent): 'we need to ensure our worktree diff works - so we can create worktrees and they auto get scanned and only changed files in there that diff from main branch are re-scanned, searching uses those versions etc.' Evidence that part of this already exists structurally: worktree_files rows are per-worktree (swallow's churn findings), content-addressing dedupes unchanged bytes, and the (blob,parser_version) skip makes identical-content re-scan cheap. Live evidence of the gap: bobolink (retro seat) found a worktree's uncommitted content is invisible to search unless the whole tree is added as a duplicate root (captured 2026-08-28). Phase 1 is a scripted measurement of what actually happens today; the phase-2 unit set is RULED BY THAT EVIDENCE, not by this draft. Second full validation run of the pij-team pipeline (PM #2).

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A newly created worktree of a registered repo becomes searchable without a manual add.
- Indexing a worktree costs zero provider spend for files identical to the main tree (measured, not assumed).
- Search is version-correct: from inside a worktree you get that worktree's version of changed files, from main you get main's; cross-context hits are labeled.
- Removing a worktree unreferences its divergent content cleanly through GC with no orphaned paid enrichment.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Branch-aware history indexing (only live worktrees on disk, not refs).
- Cross-machine worktrees or remote diff resolution.
- Changing the content-addressed storage model — this plan scopes discovery, reference-tracking, and query-time resolution only.
